title.narrative: ILF for WASH Foundational Support (IMM) for Tier Data Limited

description.narrative: Scale - TA for Impact-Linked Finance for WASH (ILF for WASH)

The **Foundational Support Programme** is one of the [++technical assistance++](https://aquaforall.org/ilf-for-wash/ilf-for-wash-technical-assistance/) tracks available for impact-driven WASH enterprises, as part of the Impact-Linked Fund for Water, Sanitation and Hygiene ([++ILF for WASH++](https://aquaforall.org/ilf-for-wash/)). The programme is supported by the [++Social Finance Academy,++](https://social-finance-academy.org/) an initiative by Roots of Impact.
The programme aims to transfer knowledge and skills from certified service providers to WASH enterprises in two areas: **impact measurement and management (IMM)** and **investment readiness (IR)**. At the same time, the goal is to embed these areas into the specific business model of the selected enterprises.
One of the selected enterprises receiving support on (only) IMM is Tier Data Limited (hereinafter referred to as 'Tier Data'), part of Centum Group, is a sector-agnostic IT provider that is expanding to a new market/sector (water) with an existing, successful product: ‘Revenu Stadia’, a cloud platform. For the water sector, they provide smart meter devices and automate efficiency, incl. centralised billing for WSPs (via their cloud platform) in water supply and distribution for last mile distributors. The enterprise installs smart meters for community water vendors; automates the billing, provides leakage detection and revenue collection.

title.narrative: Enterprise is able to systematically collect, monitor, analyse and report on impact (data).

description.narrative: Enterprise has developed an internal IMM system, i.e. i) impact strategy/Theory of Change, ii) data collection strategy/process/templates, iii) data collection and monitoring system, iv) impact/decision-making report template. Hence, the enterprise is fully prepared for the next phase (beyond the scope of this TA project), i.e. to operationalise the IMM system by developing surveys, collecting baseline (impact) data, periodically update these data, create impact reports and use them to steer operational decision-making.

comment.narrative: Despite of their commercial background, Tier Data seem to be impact-driven since they explicitly seek to focus on an underserved market segment in the water sector: CBOs (youth and women-led). They would like to integrate an impact model in their current operations. They need to start from scratch.

actual.value: All deliverables related to setting up an Impact Measurement and Management (IMM) system/process have been successfully completed, i.e.: 1) Description of problem, solutions, revenue model; 2) Impact Model and Impact Statement; 3) Customer Promise Sheet; 4) Comprehensive Theory of Change; 5) Customer Touchpoint Journey; 6) Data Collection Plan; 7) Data Analysis and Review System; 8) Decision-Making Report. The next phase (beyond the scope of this TA project) is to operationalise the IMM system, e.g. development of surveys, collection of actual data and data analysis.

title.narrative: 6.1a- Net profit margin as a percentage over time (6-months/year)

description.narrative:
Determine the number of separate operational/business units./organizations. This means the revenue generating operations of the program that will remain after program ending or separate business units that are operating under the program. In case of a franchise or connected operation falling under the same initiative you may aggregate the data and fill in one unit only
_Calculate Net profit Margin as a Percentage: Net Profit margin = Net Profit ⁄ Total revenue x 100. Net profit is calculated by deducting all company expenses from its total revenue. The result of the profit margin calculation is a percentage – for example, a 10% profit margin means for each $1 of revenue the company earns $0.10 in net profit. Revenue represents the total sales of the company in a period. Calculate over minimum of 6 months._

title.narrative: S1- Total number of current unique users served by the initiative with access to improved and safe sanitation products and services

description.narrative:
Fill in total number of unique current users for sanitation. Disaggregated per: Male/Female. Type: Domestic users (private and households), school users and for other public users (e.g markets and hospitals, communal users etc)
Finally disaggregate users that are provided with a Safely managed / Basic service / Limited service from the initiative. The initiative must tick all criteria to be considered as that service level.
1) Safely managed service:
- the initiative provides an improved sanitation facility (this includes: flush/pour flush to piped sewer system, septic tanks or pit latrines; ventilated improved pit latrines, composting toilets or pit latrines with slabs)
- the initiative's sanitation service is not shared with other households
- the initiative ensures that human excreta are safely disposed in situ or transported and treated off-site
2) Basic service:
- the initiative provides an improved sanitation facility (this includes: flush/pour flush to piped sewer system, septic tanks or pit latrines; ventilated improved pit latrines, composting toilets or pit latrines with slabs)
- the initiative's sanitation facility is not shared with other households
- initiative does not ensure that human excreta and urine is safely disposed / transported / treated
3) Limited service: Usually at baseline level, but cannot be included at target level. This includes, open pits, unimproved pit latrines, unlined pits, no slabs, prone to flooding etc
\* This is indicative of the reach and scale of the initiative in reaching new users with its products and services in terms of the service level that is being provided (as defined by JMP).
